title: Demand, duality and welfare
review_type: Specialist author mathematical, instructional, arithmetic and source review; root independently reviews and alone accepts after v05-c01

reviewed.canonical_scope: Addresses Hicksian demand, expenditure, indirect utility, Slutsky and compensating variation, with equivalent variation and quasilinear consumer surplus to distinguish income concepts. Drafted against the frozen v05-c01 prerequisite and subsequently inspected its actual D(p,m)/x(p,m) notation. Root-requested notation cleanup changed the correspondence from X(p,m) to D(p,m) throughout, preserving x for a unique choice.
reviewed.reasoning: Proved utility/expenditure attainment under stated compactness/continuity/positive-price conditions; no excess utility for attainable targets u >= U(0); both value identities and both correspondence identities under continuity and local nonsatiation. Explained scaling and ordinal invariance. Derived Shephard from the supporting cost inequality and supplied the local boundedness/uniqueness argument establishing differentiability. Derived Roy from the composed value identity, separately explained the smooth optimal-branch envelope, and explicitly required positive income and v_m > 0 rather than inferring that derivative from strict monotonicity. Derived Slutsky by chain rule, price concavity directly from minimization, Hessian symmetry/negative semidefiniteness, the price null vector and the finite compensated demand inequality. Distinguished own-price, income and cross-price restrictions with fixed arguments and units.
reviewed.welfare: Defined both CV and EV as signed losses, with positive loss/negative gain and explicit income-adjustment indifference equations. Derived exact expenditure differences and compensated integrals, identified the source's opposite signed-gain convention, and limited consumer-surplus ordering to a single price change and normality/inferiority over the full relevant range. Derived the entire two-branch quasilinear budget and expenditure functions, including continuity and failure of second-price differentiability at the join. The boundary exercise shows that an income-independent observed quantity path can coexist with a corner on the EV compensation path. Kept fixed nominal income, endogenous income, household compensation, financing and social evaluation distinct.
reviewed.worked_examples: Three original complete examples: Cobb–Douglas global AM-GM optimizer certificates and full Slutsky matrix; exact price-change welfare and old-basket upper bound; quasilinear interior/corner derivation with an exact equal-area interior case. Independently checked all numerical inputs and outputs through rational certificates, value identities and numerical integrals. No synthetic calculation is presented as an observed demand estimate.
reviewed.exercises: Solved all eight original exercises in order: matching targets/scaling and a zero-derivative ordinal transformation; attainment and two distinct failed duality assumptions; complete Slutsky/Roy calculation; Giffen versus inferior and invalid compensated matrix; weighted perfect-substitute kink; price-decrease signs and basket comparison; quasilinear compensation-path corner; and recipient-level versus total compensation. Each has a complete determinate solution and interpretation; the policy critique supplies required considerations and an illustrative feasible grant allocation. Delayed check includes answer closure. Methods are taught before use.
reviewed.sources: Retrieved actual official Alexander Wolitzky MIT 14.121 consumer-theory and applications PDFs. Inspected substantive consumer-theory pages 13–41 with budget/existence context and applications pages 3–11. Source records scope inspection and explicitly note imperfect PDF integral extraction; welfare signs and endpoints were independently derived from expenditure definitions. Did not import historical inflation estimates, source problems, or broad aggregation claims. Source IDs have v05-c02 prefixes and match the HTML's two data-source attributes.
reviewed.structure: Static HTML fragment has no h1, three aside.worked examples, one ol.exercises with eight entries, eight corresponding ordered solutions, capability/prerequisites, definitions before substantive use, assumptions/units/boundaries, teach-back, delayed check with closure, method-specific source routes and adjacent chapter links. No new lab/assets are needed for these analytic consumer cases. No framework, installation, network-dependent learning activity or visual QA claim is introduced. Root owns whole-library build and acceptance.

limitations: Author and internal root review do not constitute independent human academic certification.
The general mathematical arguments require reading; finite exact cases, differences and quadratures cannot prove all consumer-theory theorems or certify arbitrary demand systems.
Smooth derivative identities are confined to their positive-price/positive-income and differentiability conditions; kinks, zero prices, infeasible targets and satiation require separate analysis.
All examples are original synthetic divisible-good consumer models. No empirical identification of preferences, causal policy effect, current observation or interpersonal welfare measure is asserted.
General nonsmooth envelopes, demand integrability and welfare aggregation are explicitly deferred to the planned graduate extension, not represented as already supplied here.
Source verification covers the specified methods and inspected pages, not every statement in either full source document.
No visual, mobile or print UI QA was performed; the existing browser-policy restriction was respected.
Root retains shared-file integration, dependency-order acceptance, build checks and publishing responsibilities.
acceptance: Complete specialist package ready for independent root acceptance after v05-c01. Only the four assigned c02 files were written; no shared curriculum, catalogue, checkpoint, build, hosting, commits, deployment or child agents.
